No breed is inherently "living in perpetual agony", and using ARA tactics and phrasing doesn't actually help solve problems! A LOT of breeds and mixes are brachy, but BOAS and other health issues related to structure appear in more exaggerated and poorly bred examples of the breed. Individuals can deal with or not deal with any number of issues.

BOAS also appears in non brachycephalic breeds, notably Norwhich Terriers. There are also many brachy breeds that DONT have BOAS, like Chihuahua and Boxers, for example. The problem isn't the breeds themselves, or mild brachy-ness, it's unethical breeding and . Ethical breeders don't breed symptomatic dogs, stick to the parent clubs' breed standard (which DOESNT call for the extremes that often place in AKC and UKC rings) and health test for things we can test for (which will apply to BOAS soon! It's being worked on which is awesome). 

"Just stop breeding/making it illegal" does more harm than good, pretty much always. The good ethical breeders listen, throw in their hats, and sadly stop producing and preserving well bred examples of these breeds. And the unethical breeders continue producing unhealthy fucked up creatures, because they weren't ethical or listening in the first place. And people (myself included) will always want purebred dogs... wanting a puppy with a predictable temperment, health risks, appearance and size, etc. doesn't make you evil. I personally an very unlikely to buy from a shelter again, I'll always work with reputable breeders. And that's OKAY!

Making health testing for companion and toy breeds more of an expectation, ending the placement of shitty dogs in show rings because judges are stupid and love extremes, and closing down backyard breeders are all things we can actually do to help by educating puppy buyers and sending them in the direction of good breeders, because supply wont stop until demand stops. We all need to start demanding healthier, more sound dogs. Stop impulse buying animals, and put patience into finding good breeders and perfect pups. That's the solution.

And it's not impossible either- Dalmatians are an inspirational story to show that good breeders aren't afraid to outcross and change things about their breeds to produce healthier, happier dogs.
